synopsis: dSPACE’s cited vehicle-in-the-loop evidence is vendor-supplied and on-road: its intended testing chain stimulates camera, radar and ultrasound and observes responses through brakes and steering, while automotive documentation also describes camera-box limitations and downstream raw-image injection [f408, f545, f5252]. Its DARTS blog of 11 September 2019 claims radar simulation from 0.6 to 3,600 meters, 6 cm range resolution and up to five real objects in the radar test bench [f5310, f5311]. dSPACE advertises mining-truck environments with vehicle dynamics and physics-based sensor simulation, but the glossary characterizes AURELION with SIMPHERA specifically as commercial, supported by on-road-only evidence, with no public price found—leaving a gap between advertised off-road capability and the evidence identified for that package [f4126, f15895]. The booklet identifies a supported ASM–AURELION–VEOS–ModelDesk chain, OpenSCENARIO XML and OpenDRIVE support, SIMPHERA’s reliance on dSPACE ecosystem interfaces, bench integration and RoadRunner exports to dSPACE; some legacy integration technology has announced end-of-life schedules [f8704, f8616, f9205, f15897, f15999, f8894]. dSPACE benches feature in the highest-cost example chain and its real-time products are identified as computing hardware; separately, dSPACE reports that UNECE WP.29 added virtual testing to R171 at the end of 2024 [f9306, f16167, f16180, f1276].
